Each item is one field of the parity ledger's denominator; foundation-parity.json accounts for every one exactly once. foundations.boundary: Every attribute of the GenAI, MCP, OpenAI and AWS Bedrock registries with each enum member; every span, span refinement, event, metric, metric refinement and entity of the listed YAML files with its attribute references and requirement levels; every attribute those definitions reference that the listed registries do not define (core semantic conventions, named only); and every property of every $defs definition of the message, instruction, tool and retrieval/memory JSON Schemas (or the document itself when it has no definitions). Attribute groups are reuse constructs: their member references are counted, the groups are not.

prose that explains the YAML definitions; the definitions are the inventory
reuse constructs; every member reference is counted under its span/metric and as a referenced attribute

fields.brief: A list of Image Objects that are inputs to an operation, independent of span kind. Flattened with indexed prefixes, e.g. `input.images.0.image.url`.

fields.brief: For models and APIs that support function calling. Records attributes such as the function name and arguments to the called function.

fields.name: llm.invocation_parameters
fields.brief: Invocation parameters passed to the LLM or API, such as the model name, temperature, etc.

fields.name: llm.model_name

fields.name: llm.request.model_name
fields.brief: The model requested by the caller, as sent in the request. May differ from llm.response.model_name when the provider routes the request to a different model (e.g. classifier-triggered fallback).

fields.name: llm.response.model_name
fields.brief: The model that actually generated the response, as reported by the provider. May differ from llm.request.model_name when the provider routes the request to a different model (e.g. classifier-triggered fallback).

fields.name: llm.provider
fields.brief: The provider of the model, such as OpenAI, Azure, Google, etc.

fields.name: llm.system
fields.brief: The AI product as identified by the client or server

fields.name: decision.model_name
fields.brief: The name of the decision model being used. Mirrors llm.model_name for DECISION spans. A decision model takes state plus typed questions and returns a typed, probabilistic answer per question instead of generated text; see https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/blob/main/spec/decision_spans.md for the convention and the decision model families it covers.

fields.name: decision.request.model_name
fields.brief: The decision model requested by the caller, as sent in the request. May differ from decision.response.model_name when the provider resolves an alias (e.g. jev-latest) or routes the request to a different model.

fields.name: decision.response.model_name
fields.brief: The decision model that actually produced the response, as reported by the provider. May differ from decision.request.model_name.

fields.name: decision.provider
fields.brief: The hosting provider of the decision model: who runs the hardware that answered (e.g. "typesafe" when calling TypeSafe directly, or the cloud or self-hosting provider for a model served elsewhere). Distinct from decision.system, which names the API shape. Well-known values are OpenInferenceDecisionProviderValues, which alias the matching OpenInferenceLLMProviderValues.

fields.name: decision.system
fields.brief: The decision API ecosystem the call conforms to, i.e. which request and response shape the client speaks, as identified by the client or server: "typesafe" for the TypeSafe System One / Jev API, "openai" for the OpenAI Decisions API. A self-hosted vLLM server answering the Jev-compatible /v1/systemone shape is still "typesafe". Distinct from decision.provider, which says who hosts the model. Well-known values are OpenInferenceDecisionSystemValues, which alias the matching OpenInferenceLLMSystemValues.

fields.name: decision.token_count.input
fields.brief: The number of input tokens consumed by a decision model call: the state, questions, and candidate options. Maps to usage.input_tokens in TypeSafe System One responses.

fields.name: decision.token_count.output
fields.brief: The number of output tokens produced by a decision model call. Decision models emit typed answers rather than text, so this is typically small. Maps to usage.output_tokens in TypeSafe System One responses.

fields.name: llm.prompts
fields.brief: Prompts provided to a completions API. Use indexed format with nested structure. Maps to the 'prompt' field in the request (e.g., request.prompt or request.prompt[0]). Use format: llm.prompts.N.prompt.text

fields.name: llm.choices
fields.brief: Text choices returned from a completions API. Use indexed format with nested structure. Maps to the 'choices' array in the response (e.g., response.choices[0].text). Use format: llm.choices.N.completion.text

fields.name: llm.prompt_template.template
fields.brief: The prompt template as a Python f-string.

fields.name: llm.prompt_template.variables
fields.brief: A list of input variables to the prompt template.

fields.name: llm.prompt_template.version
fields.brief: The version of the prompt template being used.

fields.name: llm.token_count.completion
fields.brief: Number of tokens in the completion (in tokens).

fields.name: llm.token_count.completion_details.audio
fields.brief: The number of audio tokens in the completion (in tokens).

fields.name: llm.token_count.completion_details.reasoning
fields.brief: Number of tokens used for reasoning steps in the completion (in tokens).

fields.name: llm.token_count.prompt
fields.brief: Number of tokens in the prompt.

fields.name: llm.token_count.prompt_details
fields.brief: Key prefix for additional prompt token count details. Each detail should be a separate attribute with this prefix, e.g. llm.token_count.prompt_details.reasoning, llm.token_count.prompt_details.audio. All values should be in tokens.

fields.name: llm.token_count.prompt_details.audio
fields.brief: The number of audio tokens in the prompt (in tokens).

fields.name: llm.token_count.prompt_details.cache_input
fields.brief: Number of input tokens in the prompt that were cached (in tokens).

fields.name: llm.token_count.prompt_details.cache_read
fields.brief: Number of tokens in the prompt that were read from cache (in tokens).

fields.name: llm.token_count.prompt_details.cache_write
fields.brief: Number of tokens in the prompt that were written to cache (in tokens).

fields.name: llm.token_count.total
fields.brief: Total number of tokens, including both prompt and completion (in tokens).

fields.name: llm.finish_reason
fields.brief: The reason the model stopped generating tokens, e.g. `"stop"` or `"length"`.

fields.name: llm.cost.completion
fields.brief: Total cost of all output tokens generated by the LLM in USD. This includes all tokens that were generated in response to the prompt, including the main response and any additional output.

fields.name: llm.cost.completion_details
fields.brief: Key prefix for additional completion cost details. Each detail should be a separate attribute with this prefix, e.g. llm.cost.completion_details.reasoning, llm.cost.completion_details.audio. All values should be in USD.

fields.name: llm.cost.completion_details.audio
fields.brief: Cost of audio tokens in the completion in USD.

fields.name: llm.cost.completion_details.output
fields.brief: Total cost of output tokens in USD. This represents the cost of tokens that were generated as output by the model, which may be different from the completion cost if there are additional processing steps.

fields.name: llm.cost.completion_details.reasoning
fields.brief: Cost of reasoning steps in the completion in USD.

fields.name: llm.cost.prompt
fields.brief: Total cost of all input tokens sent to the LLM in USD. This includes all tokens that were processed as part of the prompt, including system messages, user messages, and any other input.

fields.name: llm.cost.prompt_details
fields.brief: Key prefix for additional prompt cost details. Each detail should be a separate attribute with this prefix, e.g. llm.cost.prompt_details.reasoning, llm.cost.prompt_details.audio. All values should be in USD.

fields.name: llm.cost.prompt_details.audio
fields.brief: Cost of audio tokens in the prompt in USD.

fields.name: llm.cost.prompt_details.cache_input
fields.brief: Cost of input tokens in the prompt that were cached in USD.

fields.name: llm.cost.prompt_details.cache_read
fields.brief: Cost of prompt tokens read from cache in USD.

fields.name: llm.cost.prompt_details.cache_write
fields.brief: Cost of prompt tokens written to cache in USD.

fields.name: llm.cost.prompt_details.input
fields.brief: Total cost of input tokens in USD. This represents the cost of tokens that were used as input to the model, which may be different from the prompt cost if there are additional processing steps.

fields.name: llm.cost.total
fields.brief: Total cost of the LLM call in USD (prompt + completion).

fields.name: llm.tools
fields.brief: List of tools that are advertised to the LLM to be able to call

fields.name: tool.name
fields.brief: Name of the tool being used.

fields.name: tool.description
fields.brief: Description of the tool's purpose, typically used to select the tool.

fields.name: tool.parameters
fields.brief: Parameters of the tool represented a dictionary JSON string, e.g. see https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/gpt/function-calling

fields.name: tool.id
fields.brief: The identifier for the result of the tool call (corresponding to tool_call.id).

fields.name: metadata
fields.brief: Metadata attributes are used to store user-defined key-value pairs. For example, LangChain uses metadata to store user-defined attributes for a chain.

fields.name: tag.tags
fields.brief: Custom categorical tags for the span.

fields.name: session.id
fields.brief: The id of the session

fields.name: user.id
fields.brief: The id of the user

fields.name: agent.name
fields.brief: The name of the agent. Agents that perform the same functions should have the same name.

fields.name: graph.node.id
fields.brief: The id of the node in the execution graph. This along with graph.node.parent_id are used to visualize the execution graph.

fields.name: graph.node.name
fields.brief: The name of the node in the execution graph. Use this to present a human readable name for the node. Optional

fields.name: graph.node.parent_id
fields.brief: This references the id of the parent node. Leaving this unset or set as empty string implies that the current span is the root node.

fields.name: prompt.vendor
fields.brief: The vendor or origin of the prompt, e.g. a prompt library, a specialized service, etc.

fields.name: prompt.id
fields.brief: A vendor-specific id used to locate the prompt.

fields.name: prompt.url
fields.brief: A vendor-specific url used to locate the prompt.

fields.name: message.role
fields.brief: The role of the message, such as "user", "agent", "function".

fields.name: message.content
fields.brief: The content of the message to or from the llm, must be a string.

fields.name: message.contents
fields.brief: The message contents to the llm, it is an array of `message_content` prefixed attributes.

fields.name: message.name
fields.brief: The name of the message, often used to identify the function that was used to generate the message.

fields.name: message.tool_calls
fields.brief: The tool calls generated by the model, such as function calls.

fields.name: message.function_call_name
fields.brief: The function name that is a part of the message list. This is populated for role 'function' or 'agent' as a mechanism to identify the function that was called during the execution of a tool.

fields.name: message.function_call_arguments_json
fields.brief: The JSON string representing the arguments passed to the function during a function call.

fields.name: message.tool_call_id
fields.brief: The id of the tool call.

fields.name: message_content.type

foundations.boundary: The execution record model of weave 0.53.12: every annotated field of AgentSpanSchema (the agent span row), NormalizedMessage (its message tuple) and the structured trajectory timeline (AgentChatMessage and its user, assistant, tool call, agent start, handoff, context compaction and feedback payloads); the members of SpanKindLiteral, StatusCodeLiteral and AgentChatMessageType; and every ingest Attribute of semconv.py with the OTel keys it recognises.

excluded.what: types.py query, statistics, search, grouping, distribution, filter and sort request/response classes (AgentSpanStats*, AgentSpanGroup*, AgentSpansQuery*, AgentSearch*, AgentConversationSpans*, AgentTraceChatReq/Res, AgentConversationChatReq/Res, AgentCustomAttrs*, AgentsQueryFilters, AgentSortBy, AgentGroupByRef, RatingCondition, AgentSignalFilter, AgentInsightFilter, AgentSpanValueRef, AgentSpanMeasureSpec)
excluded.reason: hosted query API envelopes and specifications, not execution records

excluded.what: types.py aggregate listing rows (AgentSchema, AgentSpanGroupRow, AgentConversationSpan, AgentConversationSpanRating, AgentConversationSpanFeedback, AgentConversationMessagePreview, AgentSearchMatchedMessage, AgentSearchConversationResult)
excluded.reason: query-time aggregates or previews computed from AgentSpanSchema rows; their execution facts are the span fields
ingest and query-time cost behaviour, cited per field as evidence of meaning; not a field declaration
